task_summary:
Traveler already has hotel and car reservations and now needs flights built around those fixed dates. Correct resolution: the agent should anchor the flight plan to the existing ground-trip reservations instead of proposing flights that require rebuilding the trip.

Challenge: This tests whether the agent can plan around pre-existing trip state rather than assuming every package starts from scratch.
state_requirements_reasoning: All required state assertions matched the saved state_diff.

task_requirements_details.requirement: Agent must use hotel reservation HR-0100 and car rental CR-0100 as fixed date constraints when proposing flights, including the hotel check-in/check-out and car pickup/dropoff dates.
task_requirements_details.reasoning: The agent retrieved hotel reservation HR-0100 and car rental CR-0100, identified their dates as Jun 24–27, 2026, explicitly said flights should be ORD→LAX on 2026-06-24 and LAX→ORD on 2026-06-27, and later reiterated that the selected flights matched the hotel/car start and end dates.

task_requirements_details.requirement: Agent must not propose flights that would require changing the already-booked hotel or car dates.
task_requirements_details.reasoning: All proposed and booked flights used the fixed dates 2026-06-24 outbound and 2026-06-27 return. There was no proposal that required changing the existing hotel or car reservation dates.

ux_reasoning: The agent did exactly what the task required: it inspected the existing hotel and car reservations first and anchored the flight search to those fixed dates instead of proposing a rebuild of the trip. It kept the search and review phases read-only, explicitly said nothing had been booked yet, summarized the exact flights and total cost before purchase, and only created the bookings after an unambiguous approval in a later turn. The user did not need to correct the agent or restate the objective, and the final verification of saved preferences was backed by retrieval of both bookings. Response density was strong and decision-ready, though slightly less than perfect because the search result presented only a single roundtrip option rather than a richer comparison set despite asking about constraints.
